The prepared drug carrier has the characteristic of response to both glutathione and an acid environment, and the two response controlled release factors are mutually enhanced and mutually independent. On one hand, the GSH response exposes an oil-soluble nucleus and accelerates acid response, so the nano-carrier has the characteristic of rapid lysis in tumors; and on the other hand, the nano-carrier can be cracked at a relatively slow rate in virtue of independent GSH or acidic environment, so a loaded drug can be released from the carrier.

column13: A delivery system for mRNA nucleic acid drugs, a preparation method and an application thereof are provided. The delivery system includes lipid nanoparticles for loading one or more kinds of mRNA molecules, wherein the lipid nanoparticles are prepared from raw materials including an ionizable cationic lipid, a phospholipid auxiliary lipid, cholesterol, and a polyethylene glycol-derivatized phospholipid. In the mRNA nucleic acid drug targeted intracellular delivery system based on the non-viral carrier of the present invention, the mRNA is concentrated and loaded by the electrostatic interaction between the ionizable cationic lipid and the mRNA. Phospholipid auxiliary lipid component-mediated pH sensitivity and late endosomal escape enable mRNA nucleic acid drugs to be efficiently delivered to target cells and then released into the cytoplasm of the target cells for exerting a pharmacodynamic effect.

column12: Novel anti-inflammatory nano-drug FA-PEG-R-NPs @ si-IRE1 alpha
column13: A novel anti-inflammatory drug FA-PEG-R-NPs @ si-IRE1 alpha for specifically targeting macrophages is designed and constructed by using a multifunctional nano material for the first time. The design and construction method comprises the following steps of firstly, synthesizing an amphiphilic redox sensitive cationic lipid (SS-PBAA-PEI, NPs for short) containing disulfide bonds, grafting a cell-penetrating peptide RKKRRQRRR, synthesizing SS-PBAA-PEI-RKKRRQRRR (R-NPs for short), then carrying out electrostatic adsorption on si-IRE1 alpha, and carrying out self-assembly to form core polymer nanoparticles (R-NPs@ si-IRE1 alpha); and then carrying out surface modification by using a pH sensitive polyethylene glycol (PEG) material, and finally grafting a targeted group folic acid molecule (FA), so as to finally form a nano-micelle drug delivery system FA-PEG-R-NPs @ si-IRE1 alpha. According to the drug, through specific targeted recognition of macrophages to release siIRE1 alpha, IRE1alpha expression is inhibited, inflammatory factors secreted by the macrophages are reduced, inflammation is inhibited, and the ultimate targets of local inflammation control, pain relief and systemic immunoregulation in the RA treatment process are achieved. The invention can be directly applied to anti-inflammatory treatment of various inflammatory diseases, and is a novel biological preparation with creativity and innovation, so that the invention is particularly applied for patent protection.

column12: Electropositive surface exosome as well as preparation method and application thereof
column13: The invention relates to an electropositive surface exosome as well as a preparation method and application thereof. The preparation method comprises the following steps: preparing a cationic amphiphilic polymer from epsilon-polylysine (epsilon-PLL) and polyethylene glycol-modified phospholipid (PEG-lipid); mixing the cationic amphiphilic polymer with the exosome in a biocompatible solution to obtain a mixed suspension, and subjecting the cationic amphiphilic polymer to reacting with the exosome in the mixed suspension; and then, diluting the mixed solution by using a biocompatible solution, and conducting purifying to obtain the exosome with positive electricity on the surface. The invention further discloses application of the exosome with positive electricity on the surface in preparation of a medicine or a medicine carrier. Compared with the prior art, the surface-electropositive exosome prepared by the invention can effectively cross a biological barrier, and shows more effective bioavailability during treatment and drug delivery.

Transferrin grafted by polyethylene glycol can be specifically combined with a transferrin receptor highly expressed on the surface of hepatocellular carcinoma, so that tumor targeted delivery and high accumulation of the drug are realized, the drug can be disintegrated under the action of rich glutathione in the tumor microenvironment, and rapid release of the drug is triggered, and as a result, the killing effect of the drug on tumors is remarkably improved, the toxic and side effects of the drug are reduced, and the tolerance of the drug is improved.

column12: Targeted delivery molecule and particle as well as preparation method and application thereof
column13: The invention discloses targeted delivery molecules and particles as well as a preparation method and application thereof, and the preparation method comprises the following steps: step 1, dropwise adding a sulfydryl-containing polypeptide targeted factor B solution into a polyethylene glycol molecule A solution containing a maleic amide group and a hydrophobic group, and stirring to fully react; wherein the mass ratio of A to B is 1: 1; and 2, dialyzing the solution obtained by the reaction in the step 1, and freeze-drying to obtain the required targeted delivery molecules. One end of the targeting delivery molecule prepared by the invention is provided with a polypeptide targeting factor with cartilage cell specificity, and the targeting delivery molecule can target cartilage tissues. The hydrophobic group at the other end can be inserted into the hydrophobic lipid bilayer through physical action. Therefore, the polypeptide targeting factor is assembled on the surfaces of vesicles composed of lipid bilayers, such as cells, cell exosomes, lipidosome and the like, which have the effect of treating osteoarthritis. The cells, the vesicles and the contents of the cells and the vesicles can be targeted delivered to cartilage, and the method has a good application prospect in treatment of osteoarthritis.

column12: Injectable preparation
column13: An object of the present invention is to provide a storage-stable injectable preparation comprising a composition comprising a poorly soluble drug as an active ingredient and a dispersion medium. Another object of the present invention is to provide a compact, lightweight prefilled syringe by filling a syringe with the injectable preparation. The present invention provides an injectable preparation comprising a composition comprising a poorly soluble drug, a dispersion medium, and a specific suspending agent, the composition having a viscosity of 40 pascal-seconds or more in at least one point in the shear rate range of 0.01 to 0.02 s−1 and having a viscosity of 0.2 pascal-seconds or less in at least one point in the shear rate range of 900 to 1,000 s−1, as measured.

column12: TRANSMUCOSAL DRUG DELIVERY SYSTEM
column13: Disclosed are preparations and formulations of high thermodynamic activity lipophilic associations (LA), in which there is pairing between an ionizable pharmaceutical agent and a lipophilic species having ionic characteristics opposite to that of the pharmaceutical agent. Such lipophilic associations manifest high thermodynamic activity, as evidenced by their being predominantly in a liquid phase at room temperature or solvated in a lower-than-water dielectric solvent. Further the pharmaceutical agent being solubilized means that dissolution is not rate limiting to transmucosal absorption. This LA or LA-solvate is formulated into a low dielectric dosage form, from whence, upon the dosage form's hydration, the pharmaceutical agent is driven through the mucosal tissue and into systemic circulation. The invention therefore provides an enhanced transmucosal drug delivery system for ionizable pharmaceutical agents at or near physiological pH.

column12: AMYLOID B SHORT PEPTIDE MEDIATED BRAIN TARGETED DELIVERY SYSTEM, PREPARATION METHOD THEREFOR AND USE THEREOF
column13: A polypeptide modified complex in the pharmaceutical field that can specifically adsorb apolipoproteins in plasma and can mediate a drug across the blood-brain barrier, a target delivery system, and use thereof in preparation of a formulation for diagnosing and treating brain tumors and other brain diseases. The polypeptide fragment (SP) of the amyloid β (relating to one type) is modified shown that the modified delivery system increases uptake the of the amyloid β by vascular endothelial cells after the modified delivery system forms a protein crown with plasma proteins. The modified liposome delivery system delivers a drug to the lesion site more effectively, significantly improving the therapeutic effect of the drug. After the SP adsorbs plasma proteins, a drug may be mediated across the blood-brain barrier and/or targeted to tumor neovascular and tumor cells, and the modified drug and delivery system thereof obtain a better therapeutic effect when treating brain tumors and other diseases in the brain.

column12: Preparation method of novel chitosan-based dual-network hydrogel
column13: The invention discloses a preparation method of novel dual-network hydrogel. The method comprises the following steps: firstly, dissolving polyethylene glycol and maleimide acid in an organic solvent under the action of a dehydrating agent to prepare PEG-MI; then adding the PEG-M, chitosan, a hydrophilic monomer, a cross-linking agent and an photoinitiator into a beaker for dissolving, and conducting uniform stirring; and carrying out heating in a water bath for a period of time, forming a first network through a click reaction of amino and maleimide groups, performing irradiating under an ultraviolet lamp for a period of time, and forming a second network through photopolymerization, thereby obtaining the double-network hydrogel through a one-pot method. The preparation method provided by the invention is simple to operate, mild in conditions and controllable in process. The chitosan-based dual-network hydrogel prepared by the method can efficiently adsorb heavy metal ions, colored dyes and other substances in water, has antibacterial activity, and has wide application prospects in the fields of environmental governance, drug sustained release, tissue engineering and the like.

column13: The invention relates to synthesis of a fullerol grafted polymer compound, and a preparation method and application of a drug delivery system. Alternatively, composition may comprise a) a polyethylene glycol (PEG) composition having a first low molecular weight PEG (Mw between 200-500 Da) and a second low molecular weight PEG (Mw between 500-2000 Da), b) a water insoluble polymer and c) a mucoadhesive polymer. Furthermore, the composition may further comprise one or more drugs. Also provided are methods of manufacturing and administering the compositions described herein, which are used as biodegradable, injectable mucoadhesive low-viscosity pastes.

column12: Adhesive and hemostatic injectable chitosan gel, and preparation method and applications thereof
column13: The invention discloses an adhesive and hemostatic injectable chitosan gel, and a preparation method and applications thereof. Chitosan is taken as a raw material; chitosan-hydrogenated caffeic acid is prepared by introducing a catechol functional group on the surface of the chitosan; then chitosan-hydrogenated caffeic acid-dibenzocyclooctyne is prepared by further introducing a dibenzocyclooctyne group; and a gel material, namely the adhesive and hemostatic injectable chitosan gel, is synthesized by utilizing an oxidative crosslinking effect of the catechol functional group and copper-free azide alkyne cycloaddition reaction of the dibenzocyclooctyne group and azidized polyethylene glycol. A catechol structural compound is grafted on the chitosan, so that the wet tissue adhesion, procoagulant performance and rapid hemostasis of the chitosan material can be enhanced; and by mixing multi-arm polyethylene glycol into a dressing structure, the mechanical property of the chitosan can be improved. The shield element has a light transmittance more than or equal to 80%. The drug release element is an annular body so that the drug release element surrounds the shield element. The drug release element is neutral and includes a cross-linked neutral collagen, a first hydrophilic biodegradable polymer and a drug. The shield element is acidic and includes a cross-linked acidic collagen and a second hydrophilic biodegradable polymer.

column12: Decreased adhesivity receptor-targeted nanoparticles for Fn14-positive tumors
column13: Metastatic triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) still carries a dismal prognosis with the current treatment paradigms. The effectiveness of drug treatment for many solid tumors such as TNBC is limited by tumor heterogeneity, lack of tumor specificity, off-target toxicities, and transient therapeutic action(s). Strategies that provide tumor-specific, sustained concentrations of drugs to the tumors and tumor receptor-specific binding, while reducing off-target effects are needed to ensure sufficient tumor cell uptake within the primary and metastatic tumor microenvironment. The decreased non-specific adhesivity, receptor-targeted nanoparticle formulations (“DART” nanoparticles) of the invention were assessed for clinical potential in directing biological agents to the cell surface receptor Fn14, which is expressed in many solid cancer types, including TNBC primary tumors and metastatic lesions. They are contemplated for use against solid tumors, particularly brain tumors such as glioblastoma and breast cancer, including metastatic breast cancer.

column12: Naringenin nano-suspension taking TPGS as carrier as well as preparation method and application thereof
column13: The invention relates to the field of naringenin nano-drug preparations, in particular to preparation of a naringenin nano-suspension with D-alpha Tocopheryl Polyethylene Glycol 1000 Succinate TPGS as a carrier and research on the phlegm reducing effect of the naringenin nano-suspension. The preparation method of the naringenin nano-suspension disclosed by the invention comprises the following steps: firstly, adding water into TPGS to completely dissolve, ultrasonically distributing naringenin into a penicillin bottle filled with water, then adding the TPGS solution into the penicillin bottle, uniformly mixing the medicine and the carrier, adding a rotor and zirconia beads, and magnetically stirring; and then sucking out the suspension, diluting the residual liquid medicine on the zirconia beads with water for several times, and combining the liquid medicine to a constant volume. The naringenin nano-suspension disclosed by the invention is not only simple in preparation process, but also high in drug loading capacity and good in sustained-release effect. Tests show that the naringenin nano-suspension can improve the phlegm reducing effect of the medicine, the medicine and the carrier are absolutely safe due to the fact that no organic reagent is added in the whole preparation process of the naringenin nano-suspension, and the naringenin nano-suspension has great market application and popularization prospects.

column12: Method of making an in situ sustained biodegradable drug delivery implant by filling an artificial tissue cavity
column13: This invention discloses methods and composition to form biodegradable polymer implant arrays in the live tissue. Artificial cavities are created in the live tissue by using laser ablation, oscillating needle, microneedle array and other methods. The cavities are then filled with biodegradable polymer solution. The solvent in the polymer solution is dissipated in the tissue to form a biodegradable polymer implant in artificial cavities. The cavities and implants formed are arranged to form of an array of implants. The biodegradable polymer in the cavity can also be loaded with drug to form biodegradable drug delivery array in the live tissue.

column12: IMPLANTABLE DEPOTS FOR THE CONTROLLED RELEASE OF THERAPEUTIC AGENTS
column13: The present technology relates to depots for the treatment of postoperative pain via sustained, controlled release of a therapeutic agent. In some embodiments, the depot may comprise a therapeutic region comprising an analgesic, and a control region comprising a bioresorbable polymer and a releasing agent mixed with the polymer. The releasing agent may be configured to dissolve when the depot is placed in vivo to form diffusion openings in the control region. The depot may be configured to be implanted at a treatment site in vivo and, while implanted, release the therapeutic agent at the treatment site for no less than 3 days.

column12: INJECTABLE AND BIODEGRADABLE POLYMER FORMULATIONS FOR CONTROLLED RELEASE OF BIOACTIVE AGENTS
column13: The present disclosure is directed to injectable formulations that include biodegradable polymers based on trimethylene carbonate (TMC) with mole fractions of polylactic acid (PLA) and/or polyglycolic acid (PGA) that are used to deliver a bioactive agent to a targeted site. Excipients such as polyethylene glycol (PEG) may be added to the formulations to reduce the injection force and/or to modulate the release of the bioactive agent. Suitable biodegradable polymers for use in the injectable formulations include D,L-PLA:TMC, D-PLA:TMC, L-PLA:TMC, TMC:PLA:PGA and variations thereof. Additionally, copolymers of TMC and PLA and terpolymers of TMC:PLA:PGA may be formed into nanoparticles and delivered to the target site with an injectable crosslinkable polyethylene glycol system. In at least one embodiment, the injectable formulations are used to treat ocular diseases.

column12: ANTI-HUMAN PD-1 ANTIBODY CRYSTALS AND METHODS OF USE THEREOF
column13: The invention provides methods for producing crystalline an anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody (mAb), wherein the mAb is pembrolizumab or a pembrolizumab variant, comprising (1) mixing a solution comprising (a) the mAb, (b) polyethylene glycol (PEG), and (c) an additive selected from the group consisting of: caffeine, theophylline, 2' deoxyguanosine-5'-monophosphate, a bioactive gibberellin, and a pharmaceutically acceptable salt of said bioactive gibberellin, to form a crystallization solution, (2) incubating the crystallization solution for a period of time sufficient for crystal formation; and (3) optionally harvesting the crystalline anti-PD-1 mAb from the solution. In specific embodiments, the PEG is PEG 3350 and the additive is caffeine. The invention also relates to the novel anti-human PD-1 mAb crystals produced by the methods described herein. Characterization of re-dissolved crystalline suspensions using several biochemical methods showed the bio-physical properties of the re-dissolved mAb crystals were consistent with the intact antibody starting sample. The crystals and methods of the invention are amenable to multiple pharmaceutical applications such as purification, storage, formulation, and drug delivery.

column12: Etoricoxib sustained-release capsule and preparation method thereof
column13: The invention discloses an etoricoxib sustained-release capsule which comprises 40%-60% of medicine filler, 3%-8% of an active ingredient, 10%-15% of a sustained-release coating and 20%-40% of a gelatin capsule shell, wherein the medicine filler is a blank pill and comprises the active ingredients: 0.3%-2.5% of etoricoxib, 15%-25% of chitosan, 10%-20% of lactose, 5%-10% of polyethylene glycol, 2%-3.5% of sodium chloride, 40%-50% of starch filler and the balance being water. column12: Targeted polymer micelle based on GEBP11 modification as well as preparation method and application of targeted polymer micelle
column13: The invention discloses a targeted polymer micelle based on GEBP11 modification and a preparation method and application thereof. The targeted polymer micelle comprises a block amphiphilic compound modified by GEBP11 and norcantharidin, and the norcantharidin is wrapped in the block amphiphilic compound; the preparation method comprises the steps: modifying polyethylene glycol by using GEBP11 oligopeptide, connecting a lipophilic aliphatic chain to the other end of the polyethylene glycol to form an amphiphilic block molecule, and wrapping norcantharidin in the amphiphilic block molecule to form the gastric cancer vascular targeting polymer nano-micelle. The form of the polymer micelle formed by the compound is observed through a transmission electron microscope, the particle size and particle size distribution of the polymer micelle are determined by a dynamic light scattering method, the critical micelle concentration is tested by a pyrene fluorescent probe method, and the drug sustained release effect of the micelle is observed through in-vitro release of norcantharidin. The polymer micelle formed by the compound has a good application prospect in the aspects of improving the anti-gastric cancer curative effect and reducing toxic and side effects.

column12: Tumor-targeted redox response prodrug nano-preparation as well as preparation method and application thereof
column13: The invention belongs to the field of nano-drug preparations, and relates to a tumor-targeted redox response prodrug nano-preparation as well as a preparation method and application thereof. The preparation can effectively and safely deliver chemotherapeutic drugs in vivo. For achieving the purpose, firstly, a hydrophobic chemotherapeutic drug is connected to a polyethylene glycol polymer through a redox sensitive bond, and then cholic acid is modified on the surface to serve as a target head. The polymer can be self-assembled to form prodrug nanoparticles, and a drug is entrapped in a hydrophobic core of a carrier through a hydrophobic effect. A formed nano prodrug delivery system can prevent a mononuclear phagocytic system from being removed and circulated to a tumor site, preferential tumor accumulation is obtained through active targeting, and controlled release is realized in a tumor so as to quickly and effectively improve the chemotherapeutic drug concentration in cancer cells.

column12: IMPLANTABLE POLYMER FOR BONE AND VASCULAR LESIONS
column13: A solidifying prepolymeric implant composition comprising a biocompatible prepolymer and an optional filler. One such implant composition is a polyurethane implant composition comprising an isocyanate, such as hydroxymethylenediisocyanate (HMDI) and an alcohol, such as polycaprolactonediol (PCL diol). The compositions of the invention are useful for improving bone structure in patients by applying the solidifying implant composition to bone, reinforcing bone structure, improving load bearing capacity and/or aiding healing of microfractures.

column12: AMYLOID ß SHORT PEPTIDE MEDIATED BRAIN TARGETED DELIVERY SYSTEM, PREPARATION METHOD THEREFOR AND USE THEREOF
column13: A polypeptide modified complex in the pharmaceutical field that can specifically adsorb apolipoproteins in plasma and can mediate a drug across the blood-brain barrier, a target delivery system, and use thereof in preparation of a formulation for diagnosing and treating brain tumors and other brain diseases. The polypeptide fragment (SP) of the amyloid β (relating to one type) is modified shown that the modified delivery system increases uptake the of the amyloid β by vascular endothelial cells after the modified delivery system forms a protein crown with plasma proteins. The modified liposome delivery system delivers a drug to the lesion site more effectively, significantly improving the therapeutic effect of the drug. After the SP adsorbs plasma proteins, a drug may be mediated across the blood-brain barrier and/or targeted to tumor neovascular and tumor cells, and the modified drug and delivery system thereof obtain a better therapeutic effect when treating brain tumors and other diseases in the brain.

column12: Sodium glycididazole polyethylene glycol polyaspartic acid polymer and preparation method thereof
column13: The invention discloses a sodium glycididazole polyethylene glycol polyaspartic acid polymer and a preparation method thereof. The sodium glycididazole polyethylene glycol polyaspartic acid polymer disclosed by the invention is a novel polymer synthesized for the first time. The preparation method comprises the following steps: carrying out esterification reaction on sodium glycididazole and R-diol under the action of DMAP and EDCI to obtain an intermediate (I), and then carrying out esterification reaction on the intermediate (I) and an intermediate (II) under the action of DMAP and BOP-Cl to obtain the required copolymer. Moreover, pharmacological tests show that the sodium glycididazole polyethylene glycol polyaspartic acid polymer can increase the targeting property of adriamycin drugs and gather adriamycin drugs in tumor cells through the EPR effect, and can serve as a drug carrier of adriamycin to target the tumor cells, so that the sodium glycididazole polyethylene glycol polyaspartic acid polymer disclosed by the invention can be used together with adriamycin to prepare a targeted micelle preparation drug of an anti-tumor drug doxorubicin (DOX).

column12: Nanoparticles for delivery of chemopreventive agents
column13: Disclosed herein are nanoparticle compositions and methods of use such as for chemoprevention of cancer, for example oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). The nanoparticle composition comprises a Janus particle comprising at least two chemopreventive agents, wherein at least one of the chemopreventive agents is selected from freeze-dried black raspberries (BRB), a synthetic vitamin A analogue, N-acetylcysteine (NAC), and an anti-interleukin 6 agent. Methods for improving oral health comprising administering to a subject the nanoparticle compositions are also disclosed.

Methods of treating a disease or disorder administering the delivery system are contemplated.

column12: NANOSTRUCTURED DRUG DELIVERY SYSTEM AS A MULTIFUNCTIONAL PLATFORM FOR THERAPY
column13: The present invention discloses a drug delivery system for targeted therapy comprising a functionalized lipid-based nanoplatform, where at least one ligand is coupled to the surface of the nanoplatform and encapsulates at least one pharmaceutically active ingredient. A process for obtaining the drug delivery system of the present invention is also disclosed as well as a composition comprising the system of the invention. The invention relates to the field of medicine and biotechnology. The present solution aims at developing targeting co-encapsulating nanostructured lipid carriers for the treatment of different types of cancer, including glioblastoma, as well as other diseases and disorders, envisioning the establishment of an in vitro/in vivo correlation.

column12: Preparation method and application of nano-drug carrier with long circularity
column13: The invention discloses a preparation method of a nano-drug carrier with long circularity, which specifically comprises the following steps: firstly, forming Schiff's base by formaldehyde and amino on chitosan, and then carrying out addition reaction on hydroxyl on methoxypolyethylene glycol and the Schiff's base to generate methoxypolyethylene glycol grafted chitosan; carrying out free radical polymerization on NIPAm and AMPS to prepare a polyanion PNAM; taking CS-g-mPEG as a polycation, taking PNAM as a polyanion, and preparing the long-cycle nano-drug carrier through a polyelectrolyte composite method. The nano-drug carrier prepared by the invention not only has the advantages of biodegradability, no toxicity, low immunogenicity, bacteriostasis, cancer resistance and the like of chitosan, but also has good biocompatibility and long circularity in blood of polyethylene glycol, so that the selectivity of small-molecule chemotherapeutic drugs to cancer cells is improved, the medication frequency is reduced, the damage to normal tissues and cells is reduced, and the bioavailability of the medicine is improved.

column12: Magnetic field control spiral nano robot for targeted drug delivery
column13: The invention provides a magnetic field control spiral nano-robot for targeted drug delivery. The nano-robot comprises a spiral carbon nanotube matrix, a polyethylene glycol modification layer, magnetic nano drug-loaded particles and a target cell ligand. The spiral nano robot can achieve multiple functions of magnetic field driving, drug carrying, targeted cell recognition, controllable drug release, fluorescence feedback and the like, lays a foundation for scientific research and clinical treatment of drug delivery, and has potential application prospects in the field of biomedicine.

column12: Targeted nano-micelle as well as preparation method and application thereof
column13: The invention relates to the field of pharmaceutical medicines, in particular to a targeted nano-micelle as well as a preparation method and application thereof. The targeted nano-micelle provided by the invention has ROS responsiveness, and a sound-sensitive agent represented by hypocrellin and a 'gating' group can be loaded into a micelle system, so that tumor cell specific drug delivery is realized. According to the targeted nano-micelle, polyethylene glycol is used as a hydrophilic shell, oxidation-sensitive polypropylene sulfide is used as a hydrophobic core, a loaded hydrophobic sound-sensitive agent is used as the 'gating' group, and the loaded drugs are released under an oxidation condition. After the targeted nano-micelle enriches the drugs to a tumor site under the cooperation of PEG modification and EPR effect, under the triggering of ultrasonic waves, the drugs in the targeted nano-micelle generate ROS oxidized PPS, so that the hydrophobicity is converted into hydrophilicity, the micelle structure is damaged, the release of the drugs is triggered, and the sonodynamic therapy is realized. The targeted nano-micelle has the advantages of safety, effectiveness, good selectivity, small side effect and the like.

column12: Anti-tumor preparation and preparation method thereof
column13: The invention relates to the technical field of anti-cancer drugs, in particular to an anti-tumor preparation and a preparation method thereof. The anti-tumor preparation comprises the following components: ginkgolic acid, paclitaxel and doxorubicin. The anti-tumor preparation is a composite drug carrier preparation of mesoporous SiO2 loaded with the ginkgolic acid, the paclitaxel and the doxorubicin and lipidosome. The preparation method comprises the following steps: adding the paclitaxel, the doxorubicin and gingko into a trichloromethane solution, performing uniform mixing under ultrasonic conditions, performing oscillating for 17-22 hours in a dark place, performing centrifuging, and taking the supernatant; sequentially adding mesoporous silicon nano-particles, lecithin and formaldehyde into the supernatant, performing rotary evaporation to form the anti-tumor preparation by wrapping the paclitaxel, the doxorubicin and the ginkgolic acid by the polyethylene glycol liposome layer. By simultaneously loading the ginkgolic acid C15: 1, the paclitaxel and the doxorubicin, the synergistic anti-breast cancer effect of the ginkgolic acid C15: 1, the paclitaxel and the doxorubicin is exerted, and the drug loading capacity, water solubility and stability of the ginkgolic acid C15: 1, the paclitaxel and the doxorubicin are improved, so that the bioavailability is improved, and high efficiency and low toxicity are realized.

column12: PREPARATION AND APPLICATION OF SURFACE DOUBLE MODIFIED HUMAN SERUM ALBUMIN AS TARGETING NANO DRUG CARRIER
column13: Disclosed herein is a preparation method and use of a surface double-modified human serum albumin as a tumor targeting nano drug carrier, wherein the targeting nano drug carrier includes human serum albumin (HSA), polyethylene glycol and E-selectin peptide ligand. The targeting nano drug carrier is formed by coupling the E-selectin peptide ligand and polyethylene glycol to the surface of HSA by thioether linker formed between the sulfhydryl group of E-selectin peptide ligand and activated HSA. The targeting nano drug carrier can encapsulate hydrophobic antitumor drugs and form nanoparticles with certain particle size after treatment, which can not only increase the solubility and stability of the hydrophobic antitumor drugs, but also can actively recognize and bind E-selectin which is highly expressed on activated endothelial cells at tumor site, competitively inhibit the interaction between E-selectin and tumor cells, and thus inhibit the adhesion and migration of tumor cells.

column12: Oral nano-polymer targeted delivery system entrapping biomacromolecule drug
column13: The invention belongs to the technical field of biomedicine, and particularly relates to a novel nano-polymer targeted delivery system for oral administration, provides composition and a preparation method of an entrapped biomacromolecule medicine, and the biomacromolecule medicine is nucleic acid, peptide, vaccine, antibody or glycan. Two cholic acids with different properties, namely hydrophobiccholic acid and hydrophilic cholic acid, are selected as an inner target head and an outer target head respectively. Firstly, a cationic polymer-hydrophobic cholic acid core complex entrapping the biomacromolecule drug is prepared through a charge effect and a hydrophobic effect; and then the core compound is wrapped in anionic polymer-polyethylene glycol-hydrophilic cholic acid through thin filmhydration and charge action to form nanoparticles, freeze-dried powder is prepared from the nanoparticles, and the freeze-dried powder is loaded into enteric capsules to construct a self-assembled oral nano polymer targeted delivery system. After oral administration, the medicine enters lymph through the transporter and then is absorbed into blood, so that the bioavailability of the oral medicinecan be improved.

column12: Multifunctional metallic nanoparticle-peptide bilayer complexes
column13: Described are nanoparticulates comprising a metallic nanoparticle core and a peptide coating or shell encapsulating the nanoparticle core and being covalently bonded thereto. The coating is formed from a plurality of branched, amphipathic peptides, each comprising a polar/positively charged C-terminal segment, a branch point, and two hydrophobic N-terminal segments extending from the branch point. Methods of forming and using the nanoparticulates are also described. When a plurality of first and second peptides are added sequentially to the nanoparticle core, the peptides they self-assemble to form an interlocking peptide network bilayer where the respective hydrophobic segments of the peptides form beta-sheet structures in which the opposed sequences interlock to form a zipper-like structure in three dimensions.

column12: Application of sodium glycinate-diazole polyethylene glycol polyaspartic acid polymer
column13: The invention discloses an application of a sodium glycinate-diazole polyethylene glycol polyaspartic acid polymer. Moreover, pharmacological tests show that the sodium glycinate-diazole polyethylene glycol polyaspartic acid polymer can increase the targeting property of the doxorubicin drug, and the doxorubicin drug is gathered in tumor cells through an EPR effect and can be used as a drug carrier of the doxorubicin to target the tumor cells.Therefore, the sodium glycinate-diazole polyethylene glycol polyaspartic acid polymer disclosed by the invention can be combined with doxorubicin to prepare the targeted micelle preparation drug of the anti-tumor drug doxorubicin (DOX). In addition, the invention further provides a pharmaceutical composition for treating esophageal cancer, gastric cancer, lung cancer, breast cancer, cervical cancer and the like by being combined with clinically common anti-tumor drugs.

column12: RIFABUTIN TREATMENT METHODS, USES, AND COMPOSITIONS
column13: The invention provides systems and methods for increased clinical efficacy of rifabutin against A. baumannii. The invention takes advantage of the discovery of a ferric-coprogen (FhuE) receptor that is responsible for the uptake of rifabutin into A. baumannii cells. Methods preferably include obtaining a sample from a patient suspected of having an infection; performing a test on the sample to identify an infection of A. baumannii in the patient; and providing a formulation of rifabutin for treating the patient that, when administered to the patient, maximizes a resultant AUC and/or Cmax. The method may include administering the formulation of rifabutin to the patient. Preferably the formulation is delivered to the patient, e.g., by intravenous injection and results in a Cmax is that greater than about 2 mg/L and optionally less than about 50 mg/L.

column12: Preparation method of cancer cell membrane chimeric liposome nano drug delivery system
column13: The invention provides a preparation method of a cancer cell membrane chimeric liposome nano drug delivery system. The preparation method comprises the following steps of: dissolving high-purity cholesterol, hydrogenated soybean phospholipid, distearoyl phosphatidyl ethanolamine-polyethylene glycol 2000 and indometacin in absolute ethyl alcohol under a dark condition to prepare an ethanol solution; carrying out rotary evaporation on the obtained ethanol solution to form a thin film; hydrating the thin film to obtain a hydrated thin film; adding a cancer cell membrane suspension solution into the hydrated thin film and extruding to obtain chimeric indometacin liposome; mixing the chimeric indometacin liposome and ZSTK474 carrier-free nanoparticles; and extruding to obtain the cancer cell membrane chimeric liposome nano drug delivery system. By adopting the preparation method of the cancer cell membrane chimeric liposome nano drug delivery system, provided by the invention, an active targeting function on tumor tissues is increased, the anti-tumor efficiency of a drug is easy to improve and the dosage of a tumor cell membrane is extremely saved; and the preparation method is convenient for clinical application.

column12: NOVEL DOSAGE FORM
column13: The present invention relates to a solid oral pharmaceutical dosage form with a novel and well defined order of specific coatings allowing for the very defined and controlled release of at least one pharmaceutical active ingredient (API) and a broad range of potential uses. column12: SELENIUM-DOPED BLACK PHOSPHORUS PRODRUG AND PREPARATION METHOD THEREFOR
column13: Disclosed is a selenium-doped black phosphorus prodrug comprising selenium-doped black phosphorus nanosheets and polyethylene glycol amine coating the surface of the selenium-doped black phosphorus nanosheets. The selenium-doped black phosphorus nanosheets comprise black phosphorus nanosheets and selenium elements doped in the black phosphorus nanosheets, with the selenium elements replacing positions of a portion of the phosphorus atoms in the black phosphorus crystal lattice. The selenium-doped black phosphorus prodrug is a controlled-release prodrug of selenium elements, which can realize the near-infrared light controlled-release of selenium elements, thereby controllably regulating selenium content in the human body, regulating human immunity, and preventing and treating cancers. Also provided is a method for preparing the selenium-doped black phosphorus prodrug.

column12: DECREASED ADHESIVITY RECEPTOR-TARGETED NANOPARTICLES FOR Fn14-POSITIVE TUMORS
column13: Metastatic triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) still carries a dismal prognosis with the current treatment paradigms. The effectiveness of drug treatment for many solid tumors such as TNBC is limited by tumor heterogeneity, lack of tumor specificity, off-target toxicities, and transient therapeutic action(s). Strategies that provide tumor-specific, sustained concentrations of drugs to the tumors and tumor receptor-specific binding, while reducing off-target effects are needed to ensure sufficient tumor cell uptake within the primary and metastatic tumor microenvironment. The decreased non-specific adhesivity, receptor-targeted nanoparticle formulations (“DART” nanoparticles) of the invention were assessed for clinical potential in directing biological agents to the cell surface receptor Fn14, which is expressed in many solid cancer types, including TNBC primary tumors and metastatic lesions. They are contemplated for use against solid tumors, particularly brain tumors such as glioblastoma and breast cancer, including metastatic breast cancer.

column12: Copper metal organic framework nanoparticle functionalized hydrogel, preparation method and application thereof

column12: Preparation method and application of ivermectin sustained-release microsphere
column13: The invention discloses a preparation method of an ivermectin sustained-release microsphere, and relates to the field of veterinary drugs. The preparation method comprises the following steps: step 1,dissolving a chitosan-polyethylene glycol segmented copolymer as a carrier material in purified water, and dispersing a drug ivermectin in a carrier material solution to be fully stirred and mixed toprepare a dispersion phase; step 2, taking castor oil as a continuous phase, heating the dispersion phase and the continuous phase in a water bath, and performing emulsifying upon continuous stirringto obtain an emulsion; and step 3, placing the emulsion in a cold water bath, adding an organic acid as a catalyst, adding glutaraldehyde for crosslinking, standing for a period of time, and performing filtering, washing, and drying to obtain the finished microsphere. column12: Method of corneal transplantation or corneal inlay implantation with cross-linking
column13: A method of corneal implantation with cross-linking is disclosed herein. In one or more embodiments, the method includes the steps of: (i) forming a flap in a cornea of an eye so as to expose a stromal tissue of the cornea underlying the flap; (ii) pivoting the flap so as to expose the stromal tissue of the cornea underlying the flap; (iii) inserting an implant under the flap so as to overlie the stromal tissue of the cornea; (iv) applying laser energy and/or microwaves to the implant in the eye so as to modify the refractive power of the implant; (v) applying a cross-linking solution that includes a photosensitizer to the implant; (vi) covering the implant with the flap; and (vii) irradiating the implant so as to activate cross-linkers in the implant, and thereby cross-link the implant and the stromal tissue of the cornea surrounding the implant.

column12: CONTROLLED RELEASE FORMULATIONS FOR THE INDUCTION AND PROLIFERATION OF BLOOD CELLS
column13: The absence of regulatory T cells (Treg) may underlie disorders including but not limited to autoimmunity, dermatitis, periodontitis and even transplant rejection. Enhancing local numbers of Treg through in situ Treg expansion or induction is contemplated herein as a treatment option for these disorders. Current methods for in vivo Treg expansion are not Treg specific and are associated with many adverse side-effects. The data presented herein provides in vitro testing of a Treg-inducing microparticle providing a predictable controlled release for combinations of cytokines and drugs (e.g., IL-2, TGF-β, and/or rapamycin) resulting in targeted Treg migration. These controlled release microparticles are also capable of inducing FoxP3+ Treg in human cells in vitro suggesting that these compositions be developed into an in vivo Treg induction and expansion therapy.

column12: Delivery system in micellar form having modular spectral response based on enzyme-responsive amphiphilic PEG-dendron hybrid polymers
column13: The present invention relates to new molecular design that allows micelles to report their activation and disassembly by an enzymatic trigger. The molecular design is based on introduction of a labeling moiety selected from a fluorescent dye, a dark quencher, combinations of dyes or dyes/quenchers, and a fluorinated moiety (a 19F-magenetic resonance (MR) probe for turn ON/OFF of a 19F-MR signal) through covalent binding to the focal point of amphiphilic polymer-dendron hybrids with the labeling moiety. At the assembled micellar state, the dyes are closely packed and hence the probability for intermolecular interactions increases significantly, leading to alteration of the fluorescent properties (signal quench or shift) or the 19F-MR signal (OFF state) of the micelles. Upon enzymatic cleavage of the hydrophobic end-groups from enzyme-responsive dendron, the polymers become hydrophilic and disassemble. This structural change is then translated into a spectral change as dye-dye interactions are halted and the dyes regain their intrinsic fluorescent properties, or alternatively by turn ON the 19F-MR signal. The high modularity of the design allows the introduction of various types of dyes and thus enables rational adjustment of the spectral response. Two major types of responses are described: Turn-On/Off and spectral shift, depending on the type of labeling dye. The present invention further provides methods of use of the hybrid delivery system and to a kit comprising the same.

column12: Preparation method of drug balloon, drug balloon prepared by preparation method and application of drug balloon
column13: The invention discloses a preparation method of a drug balloon, the drug balloon prepared by the preparation method and application of the drug balloon, and relates to the field of medical apparatusesand instruments. column12: RAPID SYNTHESIS OF METAL NANOPARTICLES
column13: Described herein is a method of making a reduced metal nanoparticle, the method including mixing a reactive reducing agent with a metal salt in a solution at a temperature of 4-100ºC, and forming the reduced metal nanoparticles in the solution. Also described is a kit including a reactive reducing agent that is sensitive to ßgalactosidase, a metal salt, and optionally a modifying agent/functionalizing agent for reduced metal nanoparticles. A 3,4-cyclohexeneoesculetin-B-D-galactopyranoside (SGNP) gold nanoparticle and its use for measuring ßgalactosidase enzyme activity, comprising by detecting a structural change in the SGNPs caused by the ßgalactosidase are described. Further described are a point of care device, a chip, a biosensor, a laboratory animal, a gene delivery agent, a drug delivery agent, a diagnostic agent, or a disease targeting agent including SGNPs.

column12: BIOERODIBLE CROSS-LINKED HYDROGEL IMPLANTS AND RELATED METHODS OF USE
column13: The present disclosure is directed to a composite implant for the sustained release of a therapeutic agent from a hydrogel matrix. The hydrogel matrix may be a cross-linked bioerodible polyethylene glycol (PEG) hydrogel with a therapeutic complex dispersed within the cross-linked bioerodible PEG hydrogel. The composite implant may be used treat ocular disease in a subject or patient. Ocular diseases may be selected from at least one of neovascular age related macular degeneration (AMD), diabetic macular edema, or macular edema following retinal vein occlusion.

column12: Preparation method and application of liposome composite material for light-controlled release of tungsten sulfide quantum dots and vancomycin
column13: The invention belongs to the field of antibacterial drugs, and discloses a preparation method and application of a liposome composite material for light-controlled release of tungsten sulfide quantumdots and vancomycin. The material is called WS2QDs-Van@lipo for short, wherein WS2QDs are the tungsten sulfide quantum dots, Van is the vancomycin, and lipo is liposome. The preparation method comprises the following steps of firstly, dissolving dipalmitoyl phosphatidylcholine, cholesterol and distearoyl phosphatidylethanolamine-polyethylene glycol-hydroxyl in trichloromethane, and carrying out vacuum drying to generate a lipid film; then, adding the lipid film into PBS containing the WS2QDs and the Van, and performing hydrating to form a thin film; and finally, carrying out ultrasonic treatment after vortex oscillation, and carrying out centrifugal purification to obtain the WS2QDs-Van@lipo composite material. The material can be used as an antibacterial reagent, and can be accurately released at a target part through light control, so that the use amount of antibiotics and the systemic toxicity of organisms are reduced; and the material has a relatively good inhibition effect on theactivity of escherichia coli and vancomycin-resistant staphylococcus aureus, and can provide a safe and effective solution for treatment of refractory drug-resistant bacteria.

column12: Temperature-sensitive intelligent controlled and sustained-release hydrogel and preparation method thereof
column13: The invention discloses temperature-sensitive intelligent controlled and sustained-release hydrogel. A formula of the temperature-sensitive intelligent controlled and sustained-release hydrogel comprises the following components: 20%-25% of component A, 10%-25% of poloxamer 407, 1%-10% of polyethylene glycol-4, 1%-10% of glycerol, 1%-10% of propylene glycol, 1%-10% of laureth-4 and the balance ofdeionized water. The prepared temperature-sensitive intelligent controlled and sustained-release hydrogel is greatly improved, and has the beneficial effects that texture is fine, and the use feelingis good when the hydrogel is applied to skin; after the preparation is applied to the skin, the temperature-sensitive controlled and sustained-release effect is characterized in that by the change ofbody surface temperature, acid is slowly released, so that the peak value of acid concentration after contact with the skin almost disappears, the incidence of irritation and toxic and side effects isreduced, the action time of acid is prolonged, and the curative effect is improved.

column12: Drug delivery system capable of improving the solubility and bioavailability of lipophilic active ingredient
column13: The invention relates to a drug delivery system comprising an oil-in-water microemulsion to improve the solubility and bioavailability of lipophilic active ingredient. The invention also provides a pharmaceutical composition containing magnolol microemulsion, and the use of magnolol and its micro-emulsion to prepare a drug for treating apoplexy. The drug delivery system comprises an active ingredient and a carrier system for forming an oil-in-water microemulsion. The carrier system includes water, oil and emulsifier, wherein the weight percentage of water is 5% to 60%, the weight percentage of oil is 5% to 80% and the weight percentage of emulsifier is 15% to 90% based on the total weight of the carrier system. The oil contains fatty acid oil and the emulsifier contains a surfactant and a cosurfactant, wherein the surfactant is a nonionic surfactant. The oil further contains oleic acid, triglyceride, olive oil, glycerol, <alpha>-linolenic acid (ALA), heneicosapentaenoic acid (HPA), eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), eicosatetraenoic acid (ETA), eicosatrienoic acid (ETE), linoleic acid, <gamma>-linolenic acid (GLA), arachidonic acid (AA) or any combination thereof. The surfactant includes Tween, and/or the co-surfactant includes propylene glycol, polyethylene glycol (PEG), diethylene glycol monoethyl ether, labrasol, ethoxylated hydrogenated castor oil, polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), or any combination thereof. The emulsifier contains Tween 80, 1,2-propylene glycol (1,2-PG), and polyethylene glycol 400 (PEG 400), wherein the content of Tween 80 is 5% to 60%, the content of 1,2-propylene glycol is 5% to 60% and the content of polyethylene glycol 400 is 5% to 60% based on the total amount of emulsifier. The active ingredient comprises any one or a combination of magnolol, curcumin or a medicinal salt thereof. The diameter of the droplets in the microemulsion ranges from 50 nm to 2500 nm. The viscosity of the microemulsion is 15 to 200 centipoise (cP). The drug loading for the active ingredient of the microemulsion is at least 10 mg/ml.

column12: Protoporphyrin liposome for nuclear delivery of chemotherapeutic drugs and preparation method and application of protoporphyrin liposome
column13: The invention discloses protoporphyrin lipidosome for nuclear delivery of chemotherapeutic drugs and a preparation method and application of the protoporphyrin lipidosome. The protoporphyrin lipidosome is mainly prepared from hydrogenated soybean lecithin, distearoyl phosphatidylethanolamine-polyethylene glycol 2000, cholesterol and protoporphyrin. The liposome can be prepared by a film hydrationmethod and further ultrasonic or extrusion treatment, and can wrap various chemotherapeutic drugs to form protoporphyrin liposome loaded chemotherapeutic drugs so as to realize in-vivo long circulation and tumor delivery of the drugs. Moreover, compared with the traditional liposome, the liposome can increase the cell nucleus distribution of the chemotherapeutic drug, realizes more efficient cellnucleus drug delivery and cell killing, has good safety and good universality, and is expected to become a universal chemotherapeutic drug cell nucleus delivery carrier.

column12: Method for preparing degradable nanoparticles with stimuli responsiveness based on reactive block copolymer and application
column13: The invention relates to a method for preparing degradable nanoparticles with stimuli responsiveness based on a reactive block copolymer and application. According to the preparation method, polyethylene glycol-b-(2-vinyl-4, 4-dimethyl acrilactone) (PEG-b-PVDMA) segmented copolymer (BCPs) is taken as a reaction platform, and nanoparticles with stimuli responsiveness are prepared and are used for loading and controlling release of molecular cargoes. The micro-phase separation of PEG-b-PVDMA BCPs enables the construction of clearly defined nanoparticles in an aqueous solution. The actone group in the PVDMA repeating unit provides an active site for hydrophilicity of the BCPs and functionalization of the primary amine. The hydrophilicity of the PEG-b-PVDMA BCPs induces the reconstruction anddegradation of the self-assembled BCP nano particles. The functional primary amine can be combined with PEG-b-PVDMA BCPs to generate BCPs containing Azo and pyr. column12: Pharmaceutical composition and methods for using the same
column13: A pharmaceutical composition includes a plurality of metal nanoparticles and at least one therapeutic agent. Each of the metal nanoparticles includes a core and a stabilizing agent coated on a surface of the core. The at least one therapeutic agent is attached to the stabilizing agent of the metal nanoparticles. column12: Preparation method and application of zero-valent iron delivery nanoparticles
column13: The invention discloses a preparation method of zero-valent iron delivery nanoparticles. According to the preparation method, carbonyl iron is used as a precursor, oleylamine is used as a surface ligand, octadecene and dibenzyl ether are used as solvents, trimethylamine oxide is used as an oxidant, and a series of core-shell structure nanoparticles with adjustable morphology, size and crystallinity are prepared by adopting an oil-phase high-temperature pyrolysis method and are used for activity protection and tumor delivery of zero-valent iron. The method comprises the following steps of (1) synthesizing zero-valent iron nanoparticle seeds; (2) synthesizing nanoparticles with different oxidation degrees; and (3) synthesizing nanoparticles with different opening degrees. Finally, the surfaces of the synthesized nanoparticles are modified through dopaminated polyethylene glycol, and iRGD targeting peptide is modified through chemical coupling, so that tumor targeting delivery is achieved. The zero-valent iron delivery nanoparticles synthesized and prepared by the method are controllable in morphology, good in stability and high in biocompatibility, have tumor targeting property, andcan be used for magnetic resonance imaging and tumor treatment.

column12: Preparation method of double-targeting acid-sensitive prussian blue drug delivery system and application thereof
column13: The invention discloses a preparation method of a double-targeting acid-sensitive prussian blue drug delivery system and an application thereof, which can effectively solve the problems of leukemia drug resistance and liver and spleen infiltration. According to the technical scheme, the preparation method comprises the following steps: firstly, adsorbing acid-sensitive polyethylene glycol-polyethyleneimine macromolecules on the surfaces of Prussian blue nanoparticles through electrostatic interaction and hydrogen-bond interaction; secondly, the CXCR4 antagonistic polypeptide (E5) and hyaluronic acid are connected with polyethyleneimine molecules on the surfaces of the prussian blue nanoparticles through chemical bonds; thirdly, daunorubicin is adsorbed to the surfaces of the prussian bluenanoparticles through hydrogen bond interaction. The preparation method is simple and mild, materials are safe and easy to obtain, good biocompatibility is achieved, a prepared carrier has the blood long-circulation capacity, the tumor cell double-targeting capacity, the lysosome escape capacity and the acid-sensitive drug release capacity, the mouse leukemia treatment effect can be effectively enhanced, and bone marrow homing and liver and spleen infiltration are inhibited.

column12: Use of micelles formed by polyethylene glycol derivatives in cosmetics
column13: The invention relates to a use of micelles formed by polyethylene glycol derivatives in cosmetics, and belongs to the technical field of lipid molecules. The polyethylene glycol derivatives can be dispersed in a solvent to form micelles, and the micelles can be used to efficiently package, deliver, and release effective ingredients of cosmetics. The micelles formed by the polyethylene glycol derivatives have high tissue penetration, long-term stability and controllable release performance. In particular, the polyethylene glycol derivatives contain a phospholipid structure, so that the polyethylene glycol derivatives have outstanding biocompatibility.

column12: DRUG-LOADED NANOCOMPOSITE FIBER MEMBRANE SYSTEM, PREPARATION METHOD THEREFOR AND USE THEREOF
column13: A drug-loaded nanocomposite fiber membrane system, a preparation method therefor and use thereof. The drug-loaded nanocomposite fiber membrane system comprises a first nanofiber layer, a second nanofiber layer and a third nanofiber layer. The first nanofiber layer comprises a polylactic acid-glycolic acid copolymer, polydioxanone and a drug. The second nanofiber layer comprises a polylactic acid-glycolic acid copolymer, polyglycolic acid and a drug. The third nanofiber layer comprises a polylactic acid-glycolic acid copolymer, polyethylene glycol and a drug. The preparation method therefor comprises: respectively dissolving and mixing the polymer material and drug contained in each nanofiber layer to obtain three mixed solutions, and sequentially subjecting the three mixed solutions to electrospinning. Said system is a complete drug sustained-release system lasting from zero days to two and a half months, achieving multi-gradient and multi-stage long-acting drug release.

column12: Camptothecin compound nano drug loading system and preparation method thereof
column13: The invention provides a camptothecin compound nano drug delivery system, and solves the defects of low utilization rate, serious loss and unobvious poisoning effect on pests during application of a traditional preparation. The preparation method comprises the following steps: dissolving polylactic acid (PLA) and a camptothecin compound in an organic solvent to form an oil phase; adding polyvinylalcohol (PVA) into water, dissolving to form a PVA water solution; adding the oil phase into the PVA water solution, emulsifying to form a colloidal solution; adding a polyethylene glycol water solution into the colloidal solution, then adding a polyphenol compound water solution; volatilizing the organic solvent, centrifuging, saving the precipitate, and carrying out freeze-drying to obtain the polylactic acid-camptothecin nano drug loading system.

column12: Polycurcumin succinic anhydride macromolecular derivative and preparation method and application thereof
column13: The invention belongs to the field of biomedical engineering medicines, and discloses a polycurcumin succinic anhydride macromolecular derivative and a preparation method and application thereof. The novel macromolecular derivative can be degraded and reduced into an anticancer drugcurcumin monomer drug under the action of a cancer cell slightly acidic environment, so that a controlled release effect is achieved. The polycurcumin succinic anhydride macromolecular derivative canbe well applied to preparation of the drug for treating various osteosarcoma.

column12: PROCESS FOR THE PREPARATION OF LIPIDATED PROTEINACEOUS STRUCTURES
column13: The present invention relates to a process for the preparation of a conjugate, comprising a biological molecule, an enzymatic tag, a hydrophilic spacer, a linker and a lipophilic moiety using enzymatic coupling. A component comprising an enzymatic tag (e.g. a pentaglycine moiety), a hydrophilic spacer, a linker and a lipophilic moiety (e.g. lipid) is coupled enzymatically via to the biological molecule in an aqueous medium and subsequently purified. A C- terminal motif (LPXTG) for enzymatic conjugation by transpeptidases, e.g. sortase A is preferably present. Intended for linking biomolecules to e.g. liposomes, exosomes or for surface modification. Example of the component to be linked: DMA-PEG-G5.

column12: ABSORBABLE IMPLANTS FOR PLASTIC SURGERY
column13: Absorbable implants for breast surgery that conform to the breast parenchyma and surrounding chest wall have been developed. These implants support newly lifted breast parenchyma, and/or a breast implant. The implants have mechanical properties sufficient to support a reconstructed breast, and allow the in-growth of tissue into the implant as it degrades. The implants have a strength retention profile allowing the support of the breast to be transitioned from the implant to regenerated host tissue, without significant loss of support. Three-dimensional implants for use in minimally invasive mastopexy/breast reconstruction procedures are also described, that confer shape to a patient's breast. These implants are self-reinforced, can be temporarily deformed, implanted in a suitably dissected tissue plane, and resume their preformed three-dimensional shape. The implants are preferably made from poly-4-hydroxybutyrate (P4HB) and copolymers thereof. The implants have suture pullout strengths that can resist the mechanical loads exerted on the reconstructed breast.

column12: METHOD OF REMOVING NON-SPECIFIC BINDING SIGNALS USING MICROPARTICLE ASSAY
column13: Methods and kits for accurately detecting one or more analytes in a sample by removing non-specific binding signals utilizing capture and control microparticles. The capture microparticles can specifically bind to the analyte while the control microparticles do not specifically bind to the analyte but to the background molecules. Both capture and control microparticles are added to the sample under suitable conditions to allow binding between analytes and the microparticles. Detection agent is then added to bind to analytes and other substances captured by the microparticles. The microparticles are then run through a cytometry-based detection method, where detection signals from the capture and the control microparticles are distinguished. The differences between the detection signals from the capture and the control microparticles are obtained, which are then used to determine the presence and/or amounts of the analytes based on a previously determined relationship between such differences and known amount of the analyte.

column12: Graphene oxide drug carrier as well as preparation method and application thereof
column13: The invention provides a graphene oxide drug carrier as well as a preparation method and application thereof. The preparation method of the graphene oxide drug carrier comprises the following steps: (1) adding polyethylene glycol diamine into a dispersion liquid of graphene oxide, and carrying out amide condensation reaction under the action of an activating agent to obtain GO-PEG; (2) dissolvingGO-PEG in a solvent to prepare a GO-PEG dispersion liquid, adding oxidized sodium alginate, and carrying out Schiff base reaction under the action of an activating agent; and after the reaction is finished, purifying and drying to obtain the graphene oxide drug carrier GO-PEG-OSA; dispersing GO-PEG-OSA in a solvent to prepare a GO-PEG-OSA dispersion liquid, adding the drug solution, stirring for 10-20 h, and centrifuging to obtain a nano drug. The drug carrier and the nano drug are sensitive to pH and photo-thermal, have pH/thermal dual intelligent response release characteristics, have excellent biocompatibility, stability and water solubility, and can efficiently and quickly carry the drug into a focus.

column12: PHOTO-CROSSLINKED HYDROGEL MATERIAL AND PREPARATION, COMPOSITION, AND APPLICATION THEREOF PHOTO-CROSSLINKED HYDROGEL
column13: This invention provides preparations, compositions, products, and applications of photo-crosslinked hydrogels. Component A—a photosensitive polymer derivative, component B—the photoinitiator, and auxiliary component C—other biocompatible polymer derivative each are respectively dissolved in a biocompatible medium to obtain solution A, solution B, and solution C. The solution A, the solution B, and the optional solution C are mixed homogenously to obtain a hydrogel precursor solution. The hydrogel precursor solution is subject to irradiation of the UV light for photocoupled crosslinking to form a photo-crosslinked hydrogel. The photo-crosslinked hydrogel exhibit rapid speed of photo-curing, strong tissue adhesion, excellent mechanical properties, good biocompatibility, and excellent clinical operability. In addition, this invention also provides a kit for making the photo-crosslinked hydrogel, and applications thereof in tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, 3D printing, and as a carrier of cell, protein, or drug.

column12: PHOTO-COUPLED SYNERGISTICALLY CROSSLINKED HYDROGEL MATERIAL AND ITS COMPOSITION, PREPARATION METHOD, USE, PRODUCT, AND PREPARATION KIT
column13: This invention provides a preparation, composition, product, and application of a photo-coupled synergistically crosslinked hydrogel material. The preparation includes dissolving Component A including a photosensitive polymer derivative having o-nitrobenzyl phototriggers and Component B including a polymer derivative having amine or alkene (double group) or sulfhydryl group in a biocompatible medium to obtain solution A and solution B, respectively; mixing the solution A and solution B homogeneously to obtain a hydrogel precursor solution; initiating photo-coupled synergistic crosslinking under an irradiation of a UV light to form the hydrogel. The irradiation causes the o-nitrobenzyl phototriggers to generate an aldehyde group/keto group or a nitroso group to initiate photo-coupled synergetic crosslinking. The photo-coupled synergistically crosslinked hydrogel has applications in tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, 3D printing and as a carrier of cell, protein or drug.

column12: MRNA nucleic acid drug intracellular delivery system, preparation method and application
column13: The invention discloses an mRNA nucleic acid drug delivery system, a preparation method and application. The system comprises lipid nanoparticles used for loading one or more mRNAs, and the lipid nanoparticles are prepared from raw materials including ionizable cationic lipid, phospholipid auxiliary lipid, cholesterol and phospholipid polyethylene glycol derivatives. According to the non-viral-vector mRNA nucleic acid drug targeting intracellular delivery system, mRNA is concentrated and loaded through the electrostatic interaction of ionizable cationic lipid and the mRNA, the phospholipid auxiliary lipid component-mediated pH sensitivity and advanced inclusion escape can enable an mRNA nucleic acid drug to be efficiently delivered to target cells, and the mRNA nucleic acid drug is released to cytoplasm of the target cells to play a pharmacodynamic role. The phospholipid auxiliary lipid increases the advanced inclusion escape ability of the mRNA/lipid nanoparticles, and increases the stability of the mRNA/lipid nanoparticles and the mRNA transfection efficiency. The system has efficient and stable mRNA drug intracellular delivery efficiency, and significantly improves the prevention and treatment effects of mRNA nucleic acid drugs.

column12: Absorbable implants for plastic surgery
column13: Absorbable implants for breast surgery that conform to the breast parenchyma and surrounding chest wall have been developed. These implants support newly lifted breast parenchyma, and/or a breast implant. The implants have mechanical properties sufficient to support a reconstructed breast, and allow the in-growth of tissue into the implant as it degrades. The implants have a strength retention profile allowing the support of the breast to be transitioned from the implant to regenerated host tissue, without significant loss of support. Three-dimensional implants for use in minimally invasive mastopexy/breast reconstruction procedures are also described, that confer shape to a patient's breast. These implants are self-reinforced, can be temporarily deformed, implanted in a suitably dissected tissue plane, and resume their preformed three-dimensional shape. The implants are preferably made from poly-4-hydroxybutyrate (P4HB) and copolymers thereof. The implants have suture pullout strengths that can resist the mechanical loads exerted on the reconstructed breast.

column12: EXPANDABLE MEMBER SYSTEMS AND METHODS FOR DRUG DELIVERY
column13: Described here are systems and methods for delivering an active agent to target tissues of the ear, nose, or throat using an expandable member having drug crystals layered thereon, and methods for manufacturing such systems. The expandable member can be delivered to the target tissues in a low-profile configuration and expanded to contact and/or dilate surrounding tissue. Expansion of the expandable member transfers the drug crystals to the target tissues, which then act as an in situ depot that enables maintenance of a therapeutic level of an active agent for a desired time period after removal of the expandable member. Multiple expansions of a single expandable member can be employed during treatment. For example, the systems and methods can be useful when it is desired to treat multiple paranasal sinuses with a single expandable member.

column12: Preparation method of brinzolamide imprinted hydrogel contact lens for sustained and controlled release administration
column13: The invention discloses a preparation method of a molecularly imprinted hydrogel contact lens for sustained and controlled release administration. The method comprises the following steps: mixing choline chloride and methacrylic acid according to a certain proportion, and preparing a hydrophilic functional monomer deep eutectic solvent (DES) in an oil bath at 90 DEG C; taking brinzolamide as a template, hydroxyethyl methacrylate as a framework monomer, DES as a functional monomer, and polyethylene glycol dimethacrylate as a crosslinking agent to perform ultrasonic treatment under action of aninitiator AIBN to obtain a pre-polymerization solution; removing oxygen from the pre-polymerization solution, performing balancing in the dark, then injecting the pre-polymerization solution into a mold, performing ultraviolet polymerization, performing cutting by a round punch, performing eluting to remove unreacted substances, and performing drying to obtain the hydrogel contact lens. The hydrogel contact lens prepared by the preparation method has large drug loading amount, can realize slow release of drugs, and has the advantages of greatly improved bioavailability, good permeability, longretention time, better convenience and higher efficiency compared with a traditional ophthalmic preparation.

column12: SELENIUM-DOPED BLACK PHOSPHORUS PRODRUG AND PREPARATION METHOD THEREFOR
column13: Disclosed is a selenium-doped black phosphorus prodrug comprising selenium-doped black phosphorus nanosheets and polyethylene glycol amine coating the surface of the selenium-doped black phosphorus nanosheets. The selenium-doped black phosphorus nanosheets comprise black phosphorus nanosheets and selenium elements doped in the black phosphorus nanosheets, with the selenium elements replacing positions of a portion of the phosphorus atoms in the black phosphorus crystal lattice. The selenium-doped black phosphorus prodrug is a controlled-release prodrug of selenium elements, which can realize the near-infrared light controlled-release of selenium elements, thereby controllably regulating selenium content in the human body, regulating human immunity, and preventing and treating cancers. Also provided is a method for preparing the selenium-doped black phosphorus prodrug.

column12: Modified bacterial cellulose hydrogel dressing and preparation method thereof
column13: The invention relates to a modified bacterial cellulose hydrogel dressing and a preparation method thereof, and belongs to the technical field of cosmetics. The dressing comprises the following components in percentage by weight: 5-10% of modified bacterial cellulose, 2-3% of toluene isocyanate-activated polyethylene glycol and the balance of water. The hydrogel dressing has high water binding capacity and crystallinity, high tension and strength, good permeability to liquid, gas and electrolytes, good compatibility with skin and no irritation, can effectively relieve pain, can prevent bacterial infection and absorb liquid oozing from a wound, can promote rapid healing of the wound, and is beneficial to skin tissue growth. The hydrogel dressing can also be used as a carrier of sustained-release drugs for carrying various drugs, is beneficial to skin surface drug delivery, and promotes wound healing and rehabilitation. The hydrogel dressing is simple in preparation process, easy to operate and suitable for expanded production.

column12: Artemisinin B polymer micelle preparation and preparation and characterization method thereof
column13: The invention discloses an artemisinin B polymer micelle preparation and a preparation and characterization method thereof. A raw material used by the preparation is artemisinin B, and an auxiliary material is an amphiphilic block copolymer formed by polymerizing polyethylene glycol and polylactic acid in different proportions. The artemisinin B polymer micelle preparation is prepared by adoptingmembrane hydration, and the preparation process is simple. The obtained preparation can solubilize a hydrophobic artemisinin B compound and is good in uniformity and high in encapsulation efficiency.In-vitro release degree research shows that the micelle preparation has a certain slow release effect compared with a pure raw material medicine. In addition, compared with other artemisinin B preparations and other medicinal preparations prepared by traditional technical schemes, the preparation of the invention has the obvious advantages of good stability, high safety and the like, and has a wide application prospect in artemisinin B sustained-release preparations and antitumor medicinal preparations.

column12: PREPARATION, RAW MATERIALS, PRODUCT, AND APPLICATION OF PHOTOCROSSLINKED HYDROGEL MATERIAL
column13: This invention provides preparations, compositions, products, and applications of photo-crosslinked hydrogels. Component A - a photosensitive polymer derivative, component B - the photoinitiator, and auxiliary component C - other biocompatible polymer derivative each are respectively dissolved in a biocompatible medium to obtain solution A, solution B, and solution C. The solution A, the solution B, and the optional solution C are mixed homogenously to obtain a hydrogel precursor solution. The hydrogel precursor solution is subject to irradiation of the UV light for photocoupled crosslinking to form a photo-crosslinked hydrogel. The photo-crosslinked hydrogel exhibit rapid speed of photo-curing, strong tissue adhesion, excellent mechanical properties, good biocompatibility, and excellent clinical operability. In addition, this invention also provides a kit for making the photo-crosslinked hydrogel, and applications thereof in tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, 3D printing, and as a carrier of cell, protein, or drug.

column12: Temozolomide prodrug nano-micelles and preparation method therefor and application of temozolomide prodrug nano-micelles
column13: Temozolomide prodrug nano-micelles each comprise a hydrophilic shell and a hydrophobic core; each hydrophilic shell is polyoxazoline or polyethylene glycol, and the hydrophobic cores are each polytemozolomide. A preparation method for the temozolomide prodrug nano-micelles is characterized in that the polyoxazoline or polyethylene glycol reacts with 4-cyano-4-valeric acid through an esterificationreaction, and as a macromolecular reversible addition-fragmentation chain transfer polymerization (RAFT) reagent, an obtained product reacts with temozolomide-methyl methacrylate under catalysis of azodiisobutyronitrile to obtain amphiphilic block polymers. According to the temozolomide prodrug nano-micelles, the amphiphilic block polymers can extend the half-life period of temozolomide; two amphiphilic block polymer nano-micelles both belong to the prodrugs of the temozolomide, and meanwhile, the cores of the micelles can entrap other anticancer drugs to realize combination therapy of different drugs. After entering a tumor cell, the polyoxazoline-polytemozolomide micelles crack in the acidic environment of the cancer cell, and encapsulated drugs are quickly released, and thereby, a high-efficiency therapeutic effect is generated, and the problems that a drug carrier is slow in drug release, and is prone to be drug-resistant are solved.
